requirement:
The SDK's backend integration makes the rendered prefix available to its supported
prompt-caching mechanism. The prefix includes all context, including the
question, and precedes node contents. A cache hit is not guaranteed.
The prefix fingerprint follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.agent_context`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.caching`, and I found no gap. **Prefix reaches the backend's caching mechanism, includes all context including the question, and precedes node contents** - The two backends are `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#impl[ToolAgent/Agent]` and `src/authoring/sdk.rs#impl[ReviewAgent

/Agent>]`. Both hand the prefix to the provider as its leading preamble or system text. Node inputs go in the later user message. - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[default_tool_accepts_scalar_results_and_keeps_the_exact_prefix]` asks with the context `"Question é"`, which is the question text. It asserts that `chat_history[0]` equals `Message::system("Question é")`, so the prefix is exactly the provider's leading system message and is not changed (including non-ASCII). It also asserts that `chat_history[1]` contains the node content `"source"`, so node contents come after the prefix. - `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[authoring_keeps_the_prepared_subject_snapshot_and_concrete_version]` asserts that the whole `CompletionRequest` sent by the Habeas review agent equals the expected prompt request. That request has its system text set to the prefix and the mandatory inputs in the user message. This checks the prefix-then-contents layout for the second backend. - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/validation.rs#fn[contexts_render_once_allow_non_send_values_and_hash_exact_prefix_text]` and `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/validation.rs#fn[string_and_str_contexts_deliver_identical_prefixes_and_fingerprints]` use a `MockAgent`. They assert that the delivered prefix contains every context and the question, in order and with repeats, for example `"héllo\n\npolicy\n\nquestion"`. They use several `.context` shapes: String, str, tuple, slice and Vec. They also cover node inputs from the current node and from successors, and they check the prefix is the same with and without node contents. **Fingerprint follows `agent_context`** - The fingerprint is checked against the exact delivered prefix in the same two `MockAgent` tests, via `context_fingerprint`. They cover the empty prefix, which matches an explicitly empty rendered prefix, and the prefix with a trailing question. - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/validation.rs#fn[prefix_hashes_match_known_utf8_sha256_without_normalization]` pins the versioned scheme `context-prefix-sha256-v1` and known SHA-256 values for the empty string and for `"héllo"`. It also shows that Unicode normalization and whitespace changes produce different fingerprints. - The order-sensitivity assertion on `"a\n\nb"` and `"b\n\na"` in `contexts_render_once_allow_non_send_values_and_hash_exact_prefix_text` covers order. The repeated element `("a","a")` rendering in the same test covers repetition. **Not tested** - "A cache hit is not guaranteed" is a statement, not a testable obligation. All the tests that carry the `{test}` reference to this requirement assert concrete outcomes.

text: :::{req} judge.caching
The SDK's backend integration makes the rendered prefix available to its supported
prompt-caching mechanism. The prefix includes all context, including the
question, and precedes node contents. A cache hit is not guaranteed.
The prefix fingerprint follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.agent_context`.
:::{req} agent_context
```rust,ignore
use std::borrow::Cow;
/// Reusable agent instructions, defined in trust_but_verify.
pub trait Context {
/// Supply reusable text for the beginning of the agent's prompt.
fn contents(&self) -> Cow<'_, String>;
The SDK implements this trait for the following combinations:
| Value | Rendering |
| `String` | Use its text directly. |
| `str` | Use its text directly; `&str` works through the reference implementation. |
| `&C`, where `C: Context + ?Sized` | Forward to the referenced value. |
| `[C]` and `Vec<C>`, where `C: Context` | Render elements in order, separated by two newlines. An empty collection renders an empty string. |
| Heterogeneous tuples of 2 through 12 `Context` values | Render elements in order, separated by two newlines. |
Combinations can nest and preserve repeated elements. Each `.context(value)`
call obtains the text once and retains it for both the prefix and its hash,
without retaining a borrow of `value`. The value needs no `Hash`, `Serialize`,
`Send`, or `Sync` implementation. Repeated calls use the same two-newline
separator as combinations. No context calls give the empty prefix and the
same fingerprint as an explicitly empty rendered prefix.
The cache fingerprint hashes the exact UTF-8 prefix delivered to the agent,
using a versioned scheme. It preserves order and repetition and uses neither
object addresses nor type identities. It identifies this prefix, including the
question; node inputs, the result schema, and the rest of the request are outside
that fingerprint.
